legend.summary: A slow scan line moves west to east across the night-time Earth, once per year from 2012 to 2023, then once, more slowly, across a map of how lighting changed.
legend.method: Everything you hear sits on the scan line. Stereo runs along the line: lights near the top of the map (north) sound in your left ear, lights near the bottom (south) in your right. Latitude is also pitch: the map is split into 20 bands of 6°, each with its own note, and the farther north, the higher the note. West to east is time.

items.meaning: Bright city cores, played the moment the scan line crosses them. Louder note = brighter city; the pitch and the ear it sounds in tell you how far north it is.
A low drone under everything. It swells and brightens with the total light under the line, leans toward the ear where most of that light is, and falls silent over oceans and dark land.
New or brighter lights since 2012 (purple on the map).
Lights that dimmed or went out since 2012 (orange on the map).

legend.caveat: Values are read from the colours and brightness of NASA's video frames, not from the original satellite measurements, so they are relative levels.
